sections.heading: Features of India as a developing economy

blocks.text: India is a **developing (emerging) economy** — combining the traits of underdevelopment (**low per-capita income, agrarian dependence, poverty, inequality**) with rapid growth and a large **services sector** — now the **world's 5th-largest economy** by GDP and a $3.5+ trillion economy.

rows: Below the world average, though rising; a mark of a developing economy.
**Large share in agriculture (~45% workers)** but low farm productivity.
Coexistence of **modern & traditional; organised & unorganised** sectors.
Large, young population — **demographic dividend** with unemployment/underemployment.
**Tertiary sector ~53% of GDP**; rapid but with poverty & inequality.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: India as a developing economy

items: **Features of underdevelopment/development**: low but rising **per-capita income**, dualism (traditional + modern), large **agriculture-dependent workforce (~45%)** vs its smaller GDP share (~18%), demographic pressure, poverty & inequality, informal sector (~90% of workers), capital deficiency, technological gap.
**Structural shift**: primary → **services-led** economy (services ~55% of GVA) — India skipped a full manufacturing phase; **jobless growth** concern.
**Sectoral classification**: **Primary** (agri, mining), **Secondary** (manufacturing, construction), **Tertiary/services** (trade, IT, finance).
**Economy types**: mixed economy (public + private + since-1991 market); India is now the **~5th largest economy (nominal GDP)** & 3rd by **PPP**.
**Human development gaps**: literacy, health, nutrition, gender — captured in HDI, MPI (multidimensional poverty).
Developing traits: low per-capita income, agrarian workforce, dualism, poverty, inequality.
India = 5th-largest economy; services-led; demographic dividend.

prelimsPointers: India is the **world's 5th-largest economy** (by nominal GDP), **3rd by PPP**.
**Agriculture** employs ~**45%** of workers but contributes ~**18%** of GDP.
**Services** contribute the **largest share (~53%)** of GDP.
Features of a developing economy — **low per-capita income, mass poverty, unemployment, economic dualism, income inequality**.
India has a **mixed economy** (public + private sectors).
**Demographic dividend** — a large working-age population is a growth opportunity.
Large **informal/unorganised sector** employs the majority of workers.
India = **mixed economy**; ~**5th largest** by nominal GDP, **3rd by PPP**.
Structure: **services ~55% of GVA**, agriculture ~18% GVA but ~45% of employment.
Sectors: **Primary / Secondary / Tertiary**; ~90% workforce is **informal**.
Key challenge: **jobless growth** — services-led, skipping mass manufacturing.
mainsAngles: Discuss the characteristics of India as a developing economy.

glossary.definition: An economy with low per-capita income and structural features of underdevelopment, but with growth potential.
The coexistence of modern/organised and traditional/unorganised sectors in an economy.
National income divided by population — a basic measure of average prosperity.

sections.heading: Economic development since independence & planning objectives

blocks.text: Post-independence India adopted **centralised Five-Year Plans (1951–2017)** under the **Planning Commission**, pursuing **growth, self-reliance, modernisation, social justice and equity**, before shifting to the **NITI Aayog** era of cooperative federalism in 2015.

rows: Set up by resolution; **12 Five-Year Plans (1951-2017)**; based on the **Mahalanobis model** (2nd plan).
**Growth, modernisation, self-reliance, social justice/equity, full employment, poverty reduction**.
**1991 LPG reforms**; from state-led to market-led.
**NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission (2015)**; plans ended 2017.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: planning since independence

items: **Planning Commission (1950)** → **Five-Year Plans** (modelled on the USSR); the **Mahalanobis model** (2nd Plan, 1956) stressed heavy industry (Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy); **Harrod-Domar** in the 1st Plan (agriculture, after Partition).

**Landmark plans**: 1st (agri), 2nd (industry — IPR 1956, 'commanding heights'), 5th (Garibi Hatao), 6th (economic liberalisation begins), 8th (post-1991 reforms), 11th ('inclusive growth'), 12th (last, 2012-17, 'faster, sustainable, inclusive').
**Objectives of planning**: growth, modernisation, self-reliance, social justice/equity — the four pillars.
**Shift (2015)**: Planning Commission → **NITI Aayog** (think-tank, cooperative federalism, no plan-based fund allocation); Five-Year Plans discontinued → 3-year action agenda / 15-year vision.
2nd Plan = Mahalanobis (heavy industry); objectives = growth + equity + self-reliance.
Planning Commission (1950) → NITI Aayog (2015); 12 FYPs ended 2017.

prelimsPointers: **Planning Commission** set up in **1950** (by executive resolution, not statutory).
**First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)** — **Harrod-Domar model**; focus on **agriculture**.

Long-term planning objectives — **growth, modernisation, self-reliance, equity/social justice**.
**Fifth Plan** — 'Garibi Hatao' (poverty removal).
India had **12 Five-Year Plans (1951-2017)**.
**NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission (1 Jan 2015)**.

glossary.definition: A centralised medium-term economic plan; India had twelve (1951-2017).

blocks.text: **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India, 2015)** replaced the Planning Commission as the government's **think-tank**, promoting **cooperative & competitive federalism, bottom-up planning and evidence-based policy** — without the old body's fund-allocation powers.

rows: **1 January 2015** (by executive resolution); replaced Planning Commission.
**Chairperson (PM), Vice-Chairperson, CEO, Governing Council (all CMs & LG/Administrators)**.
**SDG India Index, Aspirational Districts Programme, Atal Innovation Mission, indices (Health, Water, Innovation)**.

items: **NITI Aayog** ('National Institution for Transforming India', 1 Jan 2015): a **think-tank & advisory** body — NOT a fund-allocating/statutory body (unlike the Planning Commission).
**Structure**: Chairperson = **PM**; **Governing Council** = all CMs + UT Lt-Govs (cooperative federalism); a full-time **Vice-Chairperson, CEO & experts**.

**Functions**: policy design, cooperative & competitive federalism (state rankings/indices — SDG India Index, Health, Water, School Education, Innovation, Aspirational Districts Programme), monitoring & evaluation, knowledge hub; **no plan transfers** (that role → Finance Ministry/Finance Commission).
**Approach**: bottom-up (vs top-down), 15-year vision + 7-year strategy + 3-year action agenda; flagship — **Aspirational Districts Programme, Atal Innovation Mission**.
NITI Aayog (2015): think-tank, no fund allocation; PM chairs; Governing Council = all CMs.
Key work: SDG Index, Aspirational Districts, Atal Innovation Mission.

sections.heading: Growth vs distributive justice; HDI & India's rank

blocks.text: **Economic growth** (rise in output) differs from **development** (improvement in well-being with equity). **Distributive justice** ensures growth's benefits reach all, and **human development** — measured by the **HDI** — captures this broader progress.

rows: Growth = quantitative (GDP↑); development = qualitative (welfare, equity, capabilities — Amartya Sen).
Fair distribution of income/wealth/opportunity; inclusive growth.
Composite of **life expectancy, education (mean+expected schooling), GNI per-capita (PPP)**; 0-1 scale.
India in the **'medium human development'** category (rank ~130s of 190+).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: growth vs equity, HDI

items: **Growth vs distributive justice**: high GDP growth need not reduce inequality (**Kuznets curve**); India's growth has been unequal — top-decile wealth concentration, rural-urban & regional divides.
**Measures of inequality**: **Gini coefficient**, Lorenz curve; **poverty** — Tendulkar & Rangarajan lines, **NITI's National MPI** (based on Global MPI — health, education, living standards).

**Human Development Index (HDI, UNDP)**: composite of **life expectancy + education (mean & expected years of schooling) + GNI per capita (PPP)**; India ranks in the **'medium human development'** band (~130s of ~190 countries).
**Inclusive-growth tools**: DBT, MGNREGA, PDS, education/health spending, financial inclusion (Jan Dhan), reservation & welfare — 'growth with a human face'.
**SDGs (2030)**: 17 goals; NITI's SDG India Index tracks states.
Growth (quantitative) vs development (qualitative, Sen's capability approach).
HDI = health + education + income (UNDP); India in 'medium' category.

prelimsPointers: **Growth** is quantitative (GDP); **development** is qualitative (welfare + equity).
**Amartya Sen's capability approach** underpins human development.
**HDI (Human Development Index)** — published by **UNDP** (since 1990, Mahbub ul Haq).
HDI dimensions — **health (life expectancy), education (schooling), income (GNI per-capita PPP)**.
India is in the **'Medium Human Development'** category.
Related UNDP indices — **IHDI, Gender Inequality Index (GII), Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**.
**Inclusive growth** = growth with distributive justice (a key policy goal).
**HDI (UNDP)** = life expectancy + education + GNI per capita (PPP); India in **'medium HD'** band.
Inequality measured by **Gini coefficient / Lorenz curve**; **Kuznets curve** (growth-inequality).

mainsAngles: Distinguish economic growth from development and discuss the HDI.

glossary.definition: The UNDP's Human Development Index combining health, education and income.
Amartya Sen's view of development as expanding people's real freedoms and capabilities.
The fair allocation of income, wealth and opportunity across society.

blocks.text: **Sustainable development** meets present needs **without compromising future generations** (Brundtland, 1987). It balances **economic, social and environmental** goals — increasingly urgent given **pollution, climate change and resource depletion** — and is framed globally by the **SDGs (2015)**.

rows: **Brundtland Report 'Our Common Future' (1987)** — development meeting present needs without harming the future.
**17 Sustainable Development Goals, 169 targets (2015-2030)** — UN Agenda 2030.
**Stockholm (1972), Rio Earth Summit (1992), Kyoto (1997), Paris Agreement (2015), CoP summits**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: environment & sustainable development

items: **Sustainable development (Brundtland, 1987)** = meeting present needs without compromising future generations; three pillars — **economic, social, environmental**.
**Key issues**: air/water pollution, deforestation, biodiversity loss, climate change, e-waste, land degradation; **environmental Kuznets curve**.

**India's framework**: **Environment (Protection) Act 1986, EIA, CPCB/SPCB, NGT (2010), Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Forest Conservation Act 1980, Biological Diversity Act 2002 (NBA)**; **CAMPA** (compensatory afforestation).

**Climate action**: **NAPCC (8 missions — Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, etc.)**, SAPCCs, **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, **LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)**, **Net-Zero by 2070** (Panchamrit, COP26).
**Global**: **Stockholm (1972), Rio (1992 — UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD), Paris (2015), CoP** meetings, **SDGs**; Montreal Protocol (ozone).
Brundtland (1987) definition; 3 pillars; 17 SDGs (2015-2030).
India: Net-Zero by 2070, Panchamrit, Mission LiFE.

prelimsPointers: **Sustainable development** defined by the **Brundtland Report ('Our Common Future', 1987)**.

Milestones — **Stockholm Conference (1972), Rio Earth Summit (1992), Kyoto Protocol (1997), Paris Agreement (2015)**.
**Paris Agreement** — limit warming to **well below 2°C (aim 1.5°C)**.
